_comment: PHASE 6 — agent topology. This is a FRAGMENT, not a whole config.
The live ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json on the Mac already carries the D-015
hardening (3 plugins, 0 skills) and the D-016 exec SecretRef that resolves
gateway.auth.token from the login Keychain. Overwriting that file would
silently undo both — the gateway would come back with a plaintext token
and 64 re-enabled plugins, and nothing would report an error.
So this file is merged key-by-key per ops/PHASE6_APPLY.md, never copied
over the top.
CONTAINS NO SECRETS. Pointers only (spec 12.4).

lmstudio._comment: Loopback only. Verified with lsof: 127.0.0.1:1234, never *:1234. 'Serve on Local Network' stays off — that setting puts the model endpoint on the LAN.

_no_cloud_tier: There is no API key on this machine and api.anthropic.com stays off the
READ BEFORE ADDING ONE. The spec's cloud guards are NOT built:
reason-code gating, and the DEC-3/DEC-10 tax-and-privileged block.
Adding a key without building those first creates an unguarded path
from client NPI and tax data to a third party. The absence of a key is
not the control; the absence of the guards is the reason there is no key.

TIER-L1._comment: Reads hostile text. Zero tools. See skills/lms-classifier.

TIER-OCR._comment: Apple Vision runs first; this is the low-confidence fallback.

TIER-A._comment: Day 4 call transcripts — first thing cut if the week slips (D-014).

_comment: THREE AGENTS, ALL WITH ZERO TOOLS. This is not an oversight.
Under D-009 the LMS runs as Matthew's own macOS user, so an injected
agent would inherit his full session reach — his Messages, his iCloud,
his Keychain. The privilege boundary that was supposed to contain that
does not exist.
What replaces it: no model-facing agent can DO anything. Agents read
text and return text. Every effect — filing, naming, dedupe, task
creation, notification, sending — is deterministic Python in core/,
invoked by launchd, never by a model.
That means prompt injection can at worst produce a wrong JSON field,
which lands in the review queue. It cannot produce an action, because
there is no action to reach.
ops/verify_setup.py asserts these lists are empty at gateway start and
fails the check if any of them is not. Treat a failure as stop-the-line:
it means either this file was edited or an OpenClaw update introduced a
default-on tool (D-015: there is no default-deny for skills or plugins).

lms-orchestrator._comment: Sequences the pipeline by returning the next step as data. The step is executed by core/, which validates it against a fixed enum before acting.

lms-classifier._comment: The only agent that reads untrusted content. Constrained decoding means it cannot emit anything but the schema.

lms-drafter._comment: Writes reply text. Has no mailbox, no network, no send. Code puts the text in Gmail drafts; a Telegram tap is what sends it.

_comment: A named zone, never a UTC offset (Rec 21). An offset like -05:00 is
correct for half the year and an hour wrong for the other half, and the
failure is silent: the morning brief simply arrives at 05:30 or 07:30
from November onward and nobody connects it to a config value.
ops/verify_setup.py computes the next fire time across the November
boundary and asserts the local hour is unchanged.
ownerAllowFrom is EMPTY and that is a live gap, not a placeholder.
`openclaw doctor` reports it: 'No command owner is configured.' Until a
numeric Telegram id lands here, /halt — the sole remote kill switch
(D-005) — has no authorised sender. DM pairing lets someone talk to the
bot; it does not make them the owner.
Filled in Phase 7 from the id on Matthew's first message to the bot.
Format: ["telegram:123456789"] — the numeric id, never the @handle.
